feature: Naming a new component takes the keyboard again
summary: After Make Component you can type the name straight away again; the letters no longer go to the picture and pick tools. The same goes for any panel field that takes the keyboard when it appears.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Draw a rectangle, add some text on it, select both and press Command G.
Press Option Command K (Layer > Make Component).
Without clicking, type a name and press Return.
try.shotNote: Taken with the window behind another app, so it shows the window's background look.

try.do: Press R: the rectangle tool should come up, so the keyboard went back to the picture.
Open a video, pick a cut and scroll the right panel up a little: rows stop under Ask and View | Edit and thin out at the edge.

evaluate: Does typing right after Make Component name the component every time?
Does the panel's top edge, scrolled, still look like a soft fade rather than a hard cut?
rough: The panel's top fade is now a band of the panel's own material laid over the rows instead of the rows being faded out; at rest nothing is drawn, scrolled it reads the same in the pictures, but a very busy row may look slightly blurred rather than transparent in that 14pt band.

Other panel scrollers that fade at their edges (the layers list, the Library shelf, sections the dock shortens) still use the same kind of fade that drops typed-in-code focus; nothing on them asks for the keyboard when it appears today, so no walk fails, but it is logged on this task.
